Why exactly the Progenitors abandoned the New Worlds eons ago is a heavily debated topic. Some conspiracy theorists believe that they ascended to a higher plane of existence and that it is the destiny of all intelligent life to follow in the Progenitors' footsteps. In order to achieve a Transcendence victory, you must research all technologies and then sell a large amount of Progenitor Technology on Earth.

A diverse array of Alien species and Human powers vie for control of the New Worlds. However, none are truly dominant yet. To secure your hegemony over these New Worlds, you must be the first to take control of 50% of their total surface area and grow your population to the point where it makes up 50% of the total population of the New Worlds.
[TAB]This towering cluster of monoliths is remarkably well preserved. One can only hope that doesn't apply to its security systems as well.

[TAB]The bowels of this crumbling temple complex are home to countless bizarre idols and artworks forged of precious metal, in addition to a wealth of technological artifacts from the Progenitor homeworlds.

[TAB]Long since seized during the Progenitor conquest and overgrown by tangles of poisonous vines, this ancient complex was once of unparalleled religious significance to the aliens of the New Worlds. An alien Empire reconquering the Grand Ziggurat can gain awesome political and technological power, while Human colonies dream of sacking it for its untold stores of wealth.

[TAB]The leathery eggs atop the summit of this ancient ziggurat appear to be home to a race of venomous and semi-intelligent salamanders. Although fierce and savage, if tamed their secretions may prove an invaluable source of potent neurochemicals.
[TAB]Enormous cocoons spun of unbreakable silksteel hang from the trees nearby, home to thousands of feral spiders.

[TAB]These crumbling structures, carved of lapis lazuli and jet, bear an uncanny resemblance to those of ancient Earth, and are etched with strange four-dimensional hieroglyphics which reach below the surface of the translucent structure and fluctuate slowly with the passage of time. What mysteries could lie inside?

[TAB]This primitive yet elegant prehistoric structure is hewn from strange minerals clearly not derived from the surrounding geology. To merely approach the crumbling tower and breathe in its chalky dust is somehow... exhilarating.

[TAB]The endless tunnels carved into this desert outcrop do indeed provide a small but inexhaustible trickle of rare artifacts; media sensationalism about their contents may provide an even greater source of greedy Earth emigrants in search of treasure.
[TAB]Half bioengineering laboratory and half meditative shrine, this well-preserved complex appears to have been tended by a species of semisentient vines with mobile tendrils.

[TAB]Incredibly, this abandoned research station appears to be evidence of a failed expedition undertaken by clandestine Earth government organizations several decades before public knowledge of the wormhole to the New Worlds. Further investigation is sure to provoke a media sensation, and perhaps significant leverage over the highly placed politicians behind this well-managed coverup.
[TAB]This incongruous circle of standing stones is faintly luminous and warm to the touch. Whatever purpose could they serve?

[TAB]Inside the bowels of this ancient temple complex, cryptic glyphs and diagrams are chiseled down the inner walls of an active volcano, its jagged slopes stained with the dried blood of a dozen species. What sort of fiendish rituals went on here, and for what purpose? Decoding its eldritch mysteries may prove illuminating in many ways.

[TAB]These huge but seemingly inert stone carvings nevertheless have an unsettling presence, seeming to fix passersby with a distant gaze. Those visitors inclined to stay and meditate can often hear hollow voices whispering strange secrets that seem remembered from long ago.
[TAB]These ancient sculptures appear to be forged from a strange mineral alloy and resonate hauntingly with the slightest breeze, their pitch modulating subtly with the phases of the moons.

[TAB]Lips open in a silent howl of despair, the form of a colossal humanoid titan looms out of the surrounding rock; further study reveals that this is no carving, but the remains of an enormous being whose tissues somehow appear to have been spontaneously mineralized.

[TAB]This baleful statue casts a lambent gaze across the alien countryside. Its iconic appearance has made it the object of great veneration among certain of the numerous fringe religions and apocalyptic mystery cults of Earth. Perhaps this could be turned to some advantage.

[TAB]Decoding the hieroglyphs gouged into this ancient structure reveals the story of a long-dead alien species embroiled in a futile campaign of resistance against the Progenitors. The fortifications appear to have been suddenly abandoned - or perhaps their inhabitants were just as suddenly exterminated.
[TAB]These hard and bitter berries are difficult to digest, but popular among certain sectors for their vaguely euphoric aftereffects.
[TAB]This cluster of unusually large mushrooms appears strangely Earthlike, and may even be edible.

[TAB]These tangled masses of dense subterranean roots can significantly complicate life for local farmers, but with the proper extraction techniques can provide rich yields of a mild neurotoxin that proves surprisingly addictive.
[TAB]These placid animals are easy prey for hunting or herding, though their nutritious but stringy flesh often requires hours of irradiation before it becomes palatable.

[TAB]These arctic mammals store a form of remarkably energy-rich fat in their flesh and marrow. A single herd could often provide lifesaving sustenance for small colonies stranded in the frozen reaches of the Outer Worlds.

[TAB]These large and savage walrus-like creatures have incredibly thick hides and enormous tusks, and can prove a true challenge for even the most well-equipped hunter. For those with sufficient weaponry, the energy-rich blubber of a single bull can be sufficient to sustain a small colony for a month.
[TAB]The heavily mineralized shells of these sour-tasting shellfish appear to use organic acids to concentrate and precipitate trace metal ions from the surrounding bogs.

[TAB]Encased by strangely beautiful but razor-jawed shells holding an immense pearl which could sell for a small fortune on Earth, these large carnivorous shellfish float tauntingly in the mire, luring many a prospector to an early death. Specimens that have recently fed are particularly prized by collectors for the telltale traces of golden-red throughout their iridescent nacre.

[TAB]The rapacious swarms of vermin infesting certain New World planets proved almost impossible to exterminate. However, many of these dimly intelligent creatures shared a penchant for rooting out shiny Artifacts from hidden places, making their fetid burrows an unexpected treasure trove for less squeamish Archaeologists.

[TAB]These large albino creatures unmistakably must be distant relatives of the long-extinct elephants of Earth. As they pass Human settlements, these large, sad-eyed creatures gesture sinuously with their trunks, perhaps as if in silent reproach.
[TAB]These herds of two-toed mammals proved surprisingly easy to domesticate and were adaptable for use in a variety of basic tasks, particularly when employed by a skilled colonist or Alien Hybrid.

[TAB]These oddly misshapen semi-intelligent creatures appear to be in the early stages of evolution toward a bipedal body structure, with the beginnings of crude opposable thumbs. Initial research indicates that their genomes contain a series of unusual retrotransposons which may have been engineered to artificially boost their evolutionary rate.
[TAB]These strange-bodied beings proved a serviceable (if barely palatable) source of protein, although the spores and mycelia concentrated in their wiry carapace took lengthy cooking to detoxify.

[TAB]Although their volatile peptides need to be ingested immediately after harvest, limiting their use as an export crop, the unique properties of these luminous reeds are rumored to be so effective that some will cross a galaxy to sample them.
[TAB]This gigantic organism is believed to spread its filamentous hyphae throughout countless acres of underground soil, and proves highly resistant to conventional agricultural chemicals.
[TAB]The astonishing biodiversity of these resilient tendrils can provide versatile if meager sustenance for a growing colony.

[TAB]This ancient orbital facility is welded out of a near-indestructible polymer. While its resilience is frustrating to would-be plasteel scavengers, its spintronic relays have weathered the centuries remarkably well.

[TAB]Gaping holes in this crumbling shell of a former space station have left the decks no longer habitable, but its strategic position in low orbit can make it readily adaptable as a hydroponics platform or a waystation for orbital traders.
[TAB]This swarm of tiny satellites must be centuries old, but is a serviceable source of spare parts, and several still appear capable of functional transmissions.
[TAB]Frequently found in proximity to copper deposits, gold is in increasingly high demand as the wealthy elites of Earth hoard it against the constant debasement of government currencies.
[TAB]Frequently found alloyed with trace amounts of gold, copper is in high demand for a variety of industrial uses.

[TAB]The unusual carnelian and azurite gemstones found deep in the crust of certain New World planets are made all the more precious by the inability of Earth geochemists to synthesize convincing replicas.

[TAB]The New Worlds are littered with the ruins of an ancient civilization, dubbed the Progenitors by some. Hidden deep within the plasteel rubble are remnants of an incredibly advanced technology. The ruins are often extensively scavenged by the primitive aliens who now inhabit the New Worlds, perhaps simply using the ancient technology as ceremonial baubles, or perhaps harboring a deeper understanding than the humans realize. The remnants of a picked-over Progenitor ruin often hold heaps of durable Plasteel suitable for colonial construction.

[TAB]For the wealthier nations of Earth, the development of nuclear fusion was a partial answer to the dual problems presented by the peak oil crisis and worsening global warming. However, the technology is not as efficient as had been hoped, and requires a steady input of radioactive metals, which are now becoming depleted from Earth's crust. Upon the discovery of the New Worlds, throngs of Uranium Miners journeyed forth in search of fresh deposits of radioactive fuel. They were soon joined by enterprising Physicists, hoping to break Earth's monopoly on the refining of raw Uranium into functioning Fusion Cores.

[TAB]The plentiful natural gas deposits buried deep in the ancient crust of the New Worlds could be a valuable source of export wealth for a struggling colony. With Earth's industrial base starved for feedstocks, most Human colonists cared little that the seismic fracking necessary to extract it could often poison the nearby groundwater.

[TAB]The abundant sources of light sweet crude discovered deep in the crust of the New Worlds proved a godsend to industry, coming decades after the advent of peak oil on Earth. However, the richest oilfields were often found beneath barren desert wastelands or petrified forests far from the most habitable regions, making large-scale extraction a logistical challenge to coordinate.
[TAB]Left by a long-ago collision with a massive meteor, this enormous impact crater still carries traces of valuable metals buried deep within its crust.

[TAB]This site bears witness to the relatively recent impact of a massive meteor. Still radiating an unusual warmth, the fault lines surrounding the central core are rich in valuable metals and uranium.
[TAB]Scholars speculate that this enormous skeleton may be the remnant of a failed genetic experiment by the Progenitors.

[TAB]This enormous carapace appears to have been left by a truly colossal prehistoric arthropod. The trace radioactive metals in its exoskeleton suggest it may have functioned as some form of living power source.
[TAB]Covered with a thick layer of freezing ice, this planetoid bears several well-preserved remnants of a long-ago Progenitor outpost.
[TAB]Cunningly hidden by an ancient cloaking device, the crust of this artificial moon is riddled with subterranean tunnels and laboratories rich in the knowledge of the Progenitors.
[TAB]Little more than a hunk of barren rock, the crust and mantle of this tiny planetoid nevertheless contain rich deposits of several useful industrial metals.

[TAB]Apparently the site of long-ago Progenitor experimentation, the murky surface of this tiny planetoid seethes with toxic bacterial spores and viral particles. Although highly inimical to outside life, this primordial ooze proves to be a rich source of scientifically valuable nucleic acids and neurochemicals.

[TAB]A tiny oasis amidst the hostile environment of the New Worlds, this strangely Earthlike planetoid somehow maintains an atmosphere hospitable to Terran fauna and flora. It is rumored that discoveries of trace early hominid fossils in its crust were quickly suppressed by highly placed Earth government officials.
[TAB]The oceans and swamps of this aquatic planetoid could provide a fertile staging ground for would-be narcotraffickers to establish clandestine offworld Soma plantations.
[TAB]With its core superheated by dense deposits of radioactive metals, this rocky planetoid proves a veritable gold mine for uranium prospectors.

Where conditions are right, the microorganisms deep within alien swamps and marshes can release rich seeps of methane. These could prove detrimental to the health of nearby colonists (though when properly harvested, quite beneficial to their bank accounts.)
A testament to the Progenitors' industrial might, this gargantuan machine is composed of a rare titanium alloy. So skillful was its construction that the mine shaft appears to still be operable.

While a comprehensive understanding of the technology found within a Progenitor Keep is currently beyond the capability of Humanity or the natives of the New Worlds, that does not stop them from making some use of these structures. It can be used to produce weapons (particularly by those with knowledge of the Military-Industrial Complex) and is also a highly defensible position. A Progenitor Keep acts as a colony for combat purposes.

While a comprehensive understanding of the technology found within a Progenitor Citadel is currently beyond the capability of Humanity or the natives of the New Worlds, that does not stop them from making some use of these structures. It can be used to produce weapons (particularly by those with knowledge of the Military-Industrial Complex) and is also a highly defensible position in combat.
A Progenitor Databank is a veritable treasure trove of information regarding the Progenitors and their advanced technology. It can be used to produce research without the need for input goods.

A full understanding of the methods by which the Progenitors powered their technology is likely still several generations away. What is understood is that valuable fusion cores can be salvaged from ancient Progenitor Reactors.
Much of the technology that remains inside this Progenitor Installation is unrecognizable to us. Much more of it, however, looks like something that might fetch a nice price in the markets of Earth.

This ruined Autofabrication Plant, or Autofab, for short, currently possesses nowhere near the productive capability it had back in its glory days. This does not mean that it can no longer provide benefits to our productive industries and tool manufacturing capacity.

This ancient Industrial Complex may have substantially reduced capacity compared to the time when it was new and in good repair. Despite the current state of disrepair, it can still provide a benefit to our productive industries.
Despite being abandoned for countless generations, these dilapidated ruins still serve as a formidable defensive structure.

Scattered across the New Worlds are rings of great standing stones that appear to predate even the Progenitors. Of great spiritual significance to the aliens, a large circle could attract fervent worshipers from miles around. For the human colonists, such icons were of interest mainly for the traces of high-grade platinum at each monument's core.

In secret locations across the New Worlds lie a series of hidden bases once used in interplanetary surveillance. Alien Elders working at such a site could engineer the covert abduction of scores of human servitors from Earth.

The numerous planetoids orbiting the New Worlds were rich in resources but difficult for Earthlings or aliens to colonize. With enough technology many of these tiny moons could grow enough food to support a small population, enabling the gradual development of moon colonies that could yield rich resources for export to settlements on their home planet.

[BOLD]Strategy:[\BOLD][PARAGRAPH:1][COLOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Pastures[COLOR_REVERT] can be built on unvegetated terrain that is either flat or hilly, and where [LINK=CONCEPT_CATTLE_OR_SHEEP_BREEDING]livestock[\LINK] can be bred. The production of [LINK=YIELD_HORSES]horses[\LINK], [LINK=YIELD_CATTLE]cattle[\LINK] and [LINK=YIELD_SHEEP]sheep[\LINK] is increased on those tiles.[PARAGRAPH:2][BOLD]Background:[\BOLD][PARAGRAPH:1]Pasture is land with forage for livestock either as part of a farm or for ranching on open range, or where wild animals can graze or browse. Before factory farming, pasture was where grazing animals such as cattle and horses fed. It is still used extensively, particularly in arid regions where pasture land is unsuitable for any other agricultural production. In wetter climates pasture is valued for free range and organic farming.
Similar to some agricultural practices from Earth, Aquaculture in the New Worlds allows for marine life to be sustainably harvested for food.
The painstakingly crafted forest structures of the aliens were of little use to human colonists, but through years of cultivation could provide a bounty of resources in alien hands.

Carved from the native rock over the course of centuries, the secret tunnel systems of the aliens could extend into enormous caverns that enabled rich harvests from underground and served as excellent defenses in times of war.
By excavating an Ancient Mound, buried relics of Progenitor manufacture may be recovered and exploited by those with the right technology.

Intrepid explorers on old Earth have launched archaeological expeditions since the fall of the first ancient civilizations. The New Worlds are no different. An Intrepid Explorer working as a Laborer may construct an expedition on a source of Progenitor Artifacts, allowing archaeologists to recover these artifacts with greater efficiency.

Dwindling oil resources on Earth have resulted in oil wells becoming a rarer and rarer sight. The discovery of the New Worlds has revitalized the fossil fuel industry. Once the technology that enabled the Terran industrial revolution is adapted to handle the unique mixture of alien crude, oil wells are sure to become as numerous across the New Worlds as the stars in the night sky.
Constructed by a Hardy Laborer, a Plasteel Mill can wring additional yields of building materials from forests and ruins, forming the cornerstone of a colony's growing urban infrastructure.
Some theorists postulate that given enough time, knowledge, and effort, certain lost technologies of the Progenitors can be assembled into a massive gateway reaching into unknown dimensions.

[TAB]Although growing scarcity caused Earth's dwindling store of hydrocarbons to be mainly diverted as chemical feedstocks, the canny readaptation of old 20th-century technology allowed many colonies to develop vast advantages in heavy industry through the large-scale extraction of plentiful fossil fuels from the New Worlds' virgin crust.
[TAB]Scientific progress can, at times, be a slow and steady process. The New Worlds are a source of many ideas that will be of benefit to the scientific community.

Just before the turn of the 17th century, a shortage of lumber and firewood encouraged the expansion of coal mining. Coal began to be mined in the Americas in the early 1700s, and commercial mining occurred around 1730 in Midlothian, Virginia. Coal-cutting machines were invented in the 1880s. Before their invention, coal was mined from underground with a pick and shovel. By 1912 surface mining was conducted with steam shovels designed for coal mining.

[TAB]For much of human history, victory has gone to those with access to the finest metals. From the Bronze Age onwards, metal tools, weapons and alloys have been an inherent part of the rise of civilization, spurring conquests and construction by the world's greatest empires. And while metal mining has had an impressive history, it was not until the nineteenth century that industrial mining truly began to take root.[PARAGRAPH:1]Two reasons explain this sudden intensification in mining operations. The first was the almost daily revolutions in the production of tools and consumer items, requiring a continual source of metal to produce them. The second was that the fuel that powered the Industrial Revolution was coal, nestled deep within the earth. In modern times, enormous excavators like the Bagger 288 have made it possible to mine a pit three hundred feet long and one hundred feet deep in a day, a feat that, in the past, would have required the mobilization of nations.

After investing 100 units of Hard Currency to build an Interstellar Bank, colonists can work as an Offworld Banker to generate a return on investment in the form of additional Hard Currency profits. However, too large an increase in the supply of previously scarce Hard Currency can be self-defeating; with growing imports from offworld, metals prices may decline rapidly on Earth as the underlying economic weakness asserts itself.

Although the bizarre living bioreactors bred by the Progenitors proved extremely fragile, a detailed understanding of Xenogenetics enabled some of the most advanced human Biochemists to sustain several of these organisms in culture under controlled conditions, enabling direct production of valuable Biotech without the time-consuming harvest and refining of Xenospores.

As research into the incomprehensible technology of the Progenitors advanced, the most visionary of human Theorists were able to take their work from colonial Containment Facilities directly into the field. After capturing particularly well-preserved sites such as a Progenitor Installation, a colonist assigned to work the tile as a Theoretician can salvage usable Progenitor Tech directly without the need for processing of Artifacts inside a colonial lab.

After capturing certain rare map sites rich in neurochemicals, nations with an advanced understanding of human and alien neurochemistry can order colonists to work as a Neuroscientist, extracting valuable Narcotics directly from the map tile without the need for processing of Soma inside a colonial Narcotics Lab.

The vast centralized Reactors of the Progenitors appear to function on a principle that transcends human understanding of conventional fusion power. Armed with sufficient knowledge, the best human Physicists could work efficiently as a Quantum Physicist inside a captured Reactor, salvaging functioning Fusion Cores directly without the need for manufacture from raw Uranium.

The abandoned industrial facilities left by the Progenitors contained vast pools of metallic slurry that appeared to be composed of primitive nanobots with a limited capacity for self-assembly. With the appropriate technology, a skilled Nanotechnologist could resynthesize these nanites into versatile Tools that could be adapted for industrial uses, without the need for costly smelting and machining of raw Ore.

The strange armaments found in the Progenitors' abandoned Citadels and Keeps were seldom usable directly, their power source long since drained. With enough understanding of their lost technology, a skilled Artificer could recombine their parts directly into deadly Weapons fit for human use, without the need for time-consuming manufacture from raw Ore and Tools.

Deteriorating market conditions on Earth lured many small-time independent traders to try their hand at making a living bartering a wide variety of trade goods between the myriad spaceports of the New Worlds.

The abandoned industrial facilities left by the Progenitors contained vast pools of metallic slurry that appeared to be composed of primitive nanobots with a limited capacity for self-assembly. With the appropriate technology, a skilled Engineer can program a control matrix directing these nanites to perform construction tasks for a nearby colony, creating ships and structures directly from the surrounding environment without the need for harvesting and smelting of raw Plasteel.

The most closely guarded of Progenitor facilities are rumored to contain secrets of the Illuminati, revealing intricate Alien and Human conspiracies that intertwine the power structures of Earth and the New Worlds. A Conspirator willing to face the risks can leverage these secrets to liberate his people from the Earthbound establishment, and call upon valuable aid from among the Illuminated elites.

With understanding of the complex spintronic relay systems used by the Progenitors, human Hackers can hijack long-dormant Communications Arrays to beam data directly across the wormhole. Tapping into Earth's tightly regulated media networks can weaken the stranglehold of Earthbound governments, releasing a tide of hopeful immigrants.

The bizarre environments and allegedly boundless riches of the New Worlds served as a popular topic for sensationalist coverage by Earth media, forbidden to focus on the many problems closer to home. Only a few unique resource sites on the map provide unique opportunities in this regard; a Field Journalist willing to exploit these sites can generate a potent stream of Propaganda. Without direct access to Earth media, the alien empires cannot employ Journalists; however, their Venerable Elders can work certain areas such as Abduction Sites to plot the abduction of human servitors.

Providing Laborers with both Tools and Vehicles allows them to take advantage of heavy construction equipment and advanced machine tools, significantly speeding up the development of a sophisticated planetary infrastructure.

The term 'scientific method' developed during the 19th century, replacing religious superstition and appeals to authority with empirical evidence and demonstrable fact as the cornerstone of knowledge. The inventors of the New Worlds bring this philosophy to a new star system and into a new century.

The vast amounts of data housed in the Progenitors' vacant Libraries were recorded by the Progenitors in an alien language requiring literally millions of intricate, multicolored, three-dimensional hieroglyphs. Through decades of careful study, the most erudite human Symbologists could eventually decode a wealth of valuable data from these mysterious archives.

The inexplicable distortions surrounding the New Worlds wormhole posed a growing challenge to prior human concepts of astrophysics and space-time. With sufficient technology, Astronomers operating from New Worlds colonies in the right location could make scientific progress far exceeding that of their colleagues on Earth.

Once one of the sacred Menhirs dotted across the landscape of the New Worlds is under alien control, a Venerable Elder can work as a Ritualist to act as a powerful unifying force, producing a great surge of Liberty to free its people from the tyranny of the long-absent Progenitors.

By accessing one of the covert Abduction Sites hidden across the New Worlds, an alien Venerable Elder can work as an Abductor to coordinate the kidnapping of valuable Human servants from Earth. Once captured, the alien race must still visit Earth with a Saucer to collect its new servitors.

[COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Expert Oilmen[COLOR_REVERT] are able to draw a wealth of Fossil Fuels from any tile able to produce them. An Expert Oilman will double [COLOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Fossil Fuels[COLOR_REVERT] production in the tile where he works.

[TAB]You can assign any Colonist to work as a Refinery Worker in a [COLOR_BUILDING_TEXT]Power Plant[COLOR_REVERT] or [COLOR_BUILDING_TEXT]Oil Refinery[COLOR_REVERT] to generate bonuses to industrial production in your colony through the consumption of Fossil Fuels. Hardy Laborers are even more effective in this role.

After investing 100 units of Hard Currency to build an Interstellar Bank, local colonists can work as an Offworld Banker in Low Orbit tiles to generate a return on investment in the form of additional Hard Currency profits.
Assign Colonists to the Xenogeneticist profession to directly synthesize Biotech from tiles containing Progenitor biotechnology. A Brilliant Biochemist will have particular success at this task.

Assign Colonists to the Theoretician profession to directly salvage Progenitor Technology from tiles containing a Progenitor Installation. A Brilliant Theorist will have particular success at this task.
Assign Colonists to the Neuroscientist profession to directly synthesize Narcotics from tiles containing Progenitor Improvements. A Master Drug Runner will have particular success at this task.
Assign Colonists to the Quantum Physicist profession to directly create Fusion Cores from tiles containing Progenitor power sources. A Brilliant Physicist will have particular success at this task.
Assign a Nanotechnologist to tiles containing Progenitor industrial compounds to synthesize usable Tools from their dormant nanobots. A Master Machinist will have particular success at this task.

Assign Colonists to the Artificer profession to reverse-engineer functioning Weapons from tiles containing Progenitor munitions stockpiles. A Master Arms Dealer will have particular success at this task.

Colonists working as an Offworld Trader on a Low Orbit tile will generate a small but steady stream of profits in the form of imported trade goods from Earth. Building a Spaceport will significantly increase the profits of local Traders.
Assign Colonists to the Matrix Engineer profession to generate productive industrial output from a ruined autofab. A Professional Engineer will have particular success at this task.
You may assign a Conspirator to produce Liberty from rare Illuminated sites... or perhaps it would be best to let sleeping dogs lie.
Colonists assigned to the Hacker profession can tap into Progenitor orbital facilities such as a Derelict Satellite or Communications Array to produce Propaganda.
After acquiring a resource tile with a potential source of Propaganda, you may assign a Field Journalist to lure new colonists from Earth.
A Laborer equipped with both Tools and Vehicles can construct tile improvements and clear map features at twice the usual rate.

By assigning a colonist to the inventor profession, they will consume resources to generate idea points used to unlock technologies. The exact resources consumed depend on the technology being researched. Some technologies require a specific unit to be assigned to the inventor profession in order to be unlocked.

After seizing control of a Progenitor Datacore, assigning a Symbologist to analyze the facility can produce staggering breakthroughs in Research without consuming raw materials to recreate experiments in Research Labs. A Visionary Researcher will prove particularly adept at this demanding task.

Colonists working as an Astronomer on a Deep Space or Low Orbit tile containing scientific resources such as a Space-Time Anomaly can directly generate a steady stream of Research without consuming raw resources in a colonial Research Lab. Visionary Researchers will be particularly adept at this task.

Assign our Elders to meditate at the sacred Menhirs, where their focused minds can traverse a mystic window to the stars to plot the downfall of the Progenitors, and even call on the aid of select human Illuminati to join our cause.

Take care to seize control of the valuable Abduction Sites before they are ransacked by Earthling colonists. Therein, our Venerable Elders or select Earthling abductees will be able to plot the abduction of more Human servitors, who may be easily taken when our Saucer next visits Earth.

Some of the subterranean tunnels delved by our excavators have in fact proved to be orifices of an unspeakably vast organism.
This enormous feral arachnid is relentless both in defense of its lair and pursuit of its next meal.
Of the advanced sentient computer systems left by the Progenitors, those few that are still functional have been largely driven insane by millennia of solitude.
This hideous being can only be the result of a truly unspeakable anomaly occurring in extraterrestrial space.
Deceptively harmless at first glance, these nasty little droids appear to be part of an ancient Progenitor security system.

The product of gene splicing experiments by alien scientists, Human Hybrids could range from the beautiful to the grotesque. When successful, the hybridization of DNA gave rise to offspring who were quick to learn a variety of tasks, and prodigiously talented in shaping the natural resources of the New Worlds into the high technology of Earth. Many could use their adaptable genetic makeup to pass unnoticed into human territory.

The product of gene fusion between two alien races, Alien Crossbreeds are often infused with a feral vigor that could make them deadly on the battlefield. They can also make strong and capable laborers, but are far too wild to master the delicate workings of human technology.

Both coveted and despised by Earth potentates for their powerful and destabilizing creativity, the pure science practiced by an elite few Visionary Researchers could lead to breakthroughs that would reshape the destiny of humanity.

Just before the turn of the 17th century, a shortage of lumber and firewood encouraged the expansion of coal mining. Coal began to be mined in the Americas in the early 1700s, and commercial mining occurred around 1730 in Midlothian, Virginia. Coal-cutting machines were invented in the 1880s. Before their invention, coal was mined from underground with a pick and shovel. By 1912 surface mining was conducted with steam shovels designed for coal mining.

With their fine bodies poorly adapted to the technical labors of Earth, the most daring of alien craftsmen integrated their bodies into fusion-powered exoskeletons that proved resilient and adaptable to a variety of heavy industrial tasks.

Initially specialized for use in automotive and heavy equipment plants, the Mitsubishi X-9100 series of semisynthetic workers have become progressively more ubiquitous, and are adaptable to a variety of industrial tasks. Due to their organic brains and several other vestigial organ systems, they continue to require food for sustenance and maintain full citizenship rights.

Through traditional wisdom mingled with the application of advanced Biotech, an alien Cultivator could achieve subtle miracles amid the myriad forests of the New Worlds. The Cultivator is the only unit that can create Alien Garden improvements. When settled in a colony, he can harvest richer yields from indigenous plants and animals.

Japanese society is administered by powerful self-aware AIs capable of advanced sentient behavior. These can initially be purchased from the homeworld, but their supply is tightly limited by the Emperor to ensure his continued dominance. Though they cannot be gained through education, development of a Neural Interface can eventually allow them to be manufactured at great expense. Each AI resides in a large stationary computing cluster, and must be transported by ship or convoy to be installed elsewhere.

Although more frail at hard labor than their vigorous younger descendants, the most powerful Elders possessed vast secret knowledge and power. Through decades of meditation and the ritual use of certain powerful Narcotics, the Elders gained great skills both in directing covert Illuminati conspiracies to further the ascendancy of their race, and in organizing the abduction of human servants from Earth.

Through decades of study of Progenitor technology, the most focused and persistent of alien minds could reach a level of technological skill that approached mastery of every scientific discipline. Although behind the cutting edge of Earth in each individual discipline, the range and versatility of an alien Polymath could outmatch any human specialist.

Colonial Garrisons are small, relatively unskilled military detachments pressed into service by Earth governments to protect their offworld possessions. Additional units can be requisitioned from Earth as a serviceable line of early defense, but their gradually escalating cost and limited offensive capability will eventually necessitate the development of a colonial militia.

Formed during the early days of the Soviet Union, the Russian Special Forces (abbreviated as 'Spetsnaz' in Russian) have a hard-earned, fearsome reputation. Even after the fall of the USSR and through to the end of the 21st century, the Spetsnaz are notorious for their unyielding battlefield presence among opposing armies and for their unforgiving attitude toward their rearguard duties among soldiers serving in the regular Russian army. With Russia establishing a presence in the New Worlds, the Spetsnaz are sure to join the Russian colonies.

With skills honed over decades of ritual combat and bodies heavily modified by alien technology, the elites of the alien warrior castes could prove a deadly threat to even the most hardened human military forces.

As elegant as it is horrifying, the Progenitor Naytiba strikes fear into those foolish enough to presume to fight it. Millennia of development in martial techniques have allowed the Progenitor Naytiba to wreak untold destruction on the enemies of the Progenitors with merciless, consummate grace.

Bred by alien elders by incubating offspring with carefully prepared Xenospore extract, packs of gibbering Mutants were often used as cannon fodder in a frontal assault, their mindless ferocity overwhelming defenses that would have held off any saner foe.
"Humans constantly feel pain in their hearts. Because the heart is so sensitive to pain, humans also feel that to live is to suffer."
The robotic armatures of a Mining Vessel can extract valuable resources from the various asteroid belts and space debris scattered across the deep space surrounding the New Worlds.

The advanced but delicate instruments carried by a Science Vessel can harvest valuable research data from the strange deep space anomalies prevalent in close proximity to the wormhole, and with appropriate technology can permit successful terraforming of the noxious atmospheres common to the New Worlds' resource-rich moons.

Although colonizing the tiny planetoids orbiting the New Worlds required a huge upfront investment in time and supplies, a mature Lunar Colony could eventually yield rich resources for export to its parent settlement on the planet below.

Although relatively small and weak in combat, the versatile alien saucers were able to navigate through the heavy atmosphere of the Outer Worlds, and could often outmaneuver the heavy Earth starships limited to a single orbit by the sensitive Resonance Drives used to navigate the wormhole.

Although smaller than the commercial merchant ships of Earth, the sleek vessels of alien smugglers were often fast enough to outrun an Earthling blockade and establish sporadic trading routes with disenfranchised Third World nations.

Privateers were covertly government-sanctioned pirate ships prominent in the shipping lanes of the New Worlds. Pillaging for profit, Privateers bore no markings of their national sponsor, making it impossible to trace their employer. Successful Privateers, such as the notorious Jess Keeley in the employ of President Limbaugh, wreaked havoc among the merchant vessels of rival nations, securing for themselves and their paymasters significant wealth. In addition, the disruptive effect these naval bandits had upon the enemies did much to ensure the naval supremacy of their home nations.

Using technology developed over centuries of concealment to obscure their identity, unknown alien UFOs could strike colonial ships at any moment, bearing back precious industrial cargo to the alien homeworlds.

Alien Carrier vessels, though less physically robust than equivalent ships of Human construction, have a greater carrying capacity. The few Humans to have seen the inside of one of these Carriers and reported their observations back to Earth claim that the Carriers possess a four-dimensional interior. These claims have been dismissed by the authorities as hallucinations induced by exposure to alien substances.
Although inferior in combat to the larger vessels of Earth, the most advanced alien warships incorporated cloaking technology that was a bane to human naval strategists.

Enormous planetoid-sized vessels bristling with Progenitor weaponry and often requiring decades to construct, the massive alien battlestars were slow to venture from the orbit of their home planet, but proved lethal to all but the most determined Earthling assault.

Crude oil, coal, and natural gas: these resources have grown scarce on Earth by the late 21st century. The dwindling hydrocarbon reserves have had devastating effects on the Terran economy. Now, the Great Powers of Earth believe that the infusion of alien hydrocarbons, mined from the bowels of the New Worlds, will revitalize their faltering industries.

The aliens of the New Worlds transport precious goods between their settlements on stately palanquins, moving far more slowly than Earthling vehicles but able to remain hidden on a myriad of paths across the wilderness.
I'm sorry, Dave. I'm afraid I can't do that..
[COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Human Hybrids[COLOR_REVERT] are quick to learn, and adept in the technical knowledge of the Earthlings.

The interspecies [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Alien Crossbreeds[COLOR_REVERT] are unusually large and fierce in combat, and their mixed genetic heritage often leaves foes unable to identify the source of an attack.

Although bringing less immediate monetary dividends than the valuable goods produced by Physicists and Biochemists, the endeavors of a [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Visionary Researcher[COLOR_REVERT] can stimulate [COLOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]remarkable breakthroughs[COLOR_REVERT] in a variety of fields.

[COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Expert Oilmen[COLOR_REVERT] are able to draw a wealth of Fossil Fuels from any tile able to produce them. An Expert Oilman will double [COLOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]Fossil Fuels[COLOR_REVERT] production in the tile where he works.
To master the crude heavy industry of Earth, our traditional artisans must enmesh their bodies into fusion-powered armatures. It is a sacrifice, but there is no other way.
Construct or purchase [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Android[COLOR_REVERT] citizens to bolster our industrial might.
Train an Adept [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Cultivator[COLOR_REVERT] to create forest fertilizers that will spread the noble forests of our planet and enable great future harvests.
Construct or purchase sentient [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]AIs[COLOR_REVERT] to enable our colonies to be administered independently of the home planet.
Train a [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Venerable Elder[COLOR_REVERT] who can lead our race to independence and victory.
Adapt the lost wisdom of the Progenitors to train a [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Brilliant Polymath[COLOR_REVERT] with skills in every area of science and industry.

[COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Colonial Garrison[COLOR_REVERT] forces can be requisitioned from Earth as a serviceable line of early defense, but their gradually escalating cost and limited offensive capability will eventually necessitate the development of a colonial militia.

The [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Spetsnaz[COLOR_REVERT] replace [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Veteran Soldiers[COLOR_REVERT] in the [LINK=CIVILIZATION_DUTCH]Russian Colonies[\LINK]. While significantly more expensive, they are superior in almost every aspect - especially in logistics. They traverse rough terrain and enemy lands alike, with no additional movement costs and possess the deadly ability to strike multiple times per turn.
Train an [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Elite Warrior[COLOR_REVERT] to bolster our race's military might.
Instill the spores into our younglings, following the ancient ways. The Earthling walls will never stand against their strength!
Build a [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Mining Vessel[COLOR_REVERT] to [COLOR_MAGENTA]extract[COLOR_REVERT] [COLOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]valuable resources[COLOR_REVERT] from asteroid belts and space debris.

Build a [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Science Vessel[COLOR_REVERT] to [COLOR_MAGENTA]harvest[COLOR_REVERT] [COLOR_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT]valuable resources[COLOR_REVERT] from anomalies in deep space, and allow [COLOR_MAGENTA]terraforming[COLOR_REVERT] of moons [COLOR_WARNING_TEXT]plagued[COLOR_REVERT] by a hostile atmosphere.

Construct a [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Colony Ship[COLOR_REVERT] to found a [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_MOON_COLONY1]Lunar Outpost[\LINK] that can be worked for resources by a nearby planetary settlement. This [COLOR_WARNING_TEXT]consumes the Colony Ship[COLOR_REVERT]!

Construct a [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Saucer[COLOR_REVERT] to transport troops and materials between our planets. With our limited understanding of Human technology, we would be well served to establish limited trade with Earth and abduct Earthling servitors to further our cause.
Construct a swift [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]smuggling vessel[COLOR_REVERT] to establish offworld shipping for our goods.

[COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Privateers[COLOR_REVERT] are colonial pirates, able to raid enemy vessels, disrupt your foes' shipping lanes, and just cause general mayhem. They bear no flag, meaning that you can attack your foes without having to declare war! And if you win combat against a cargo vessel, you have the chance to steal some of the vessel's goods! Be aware, however, that this sleek-hulled ship can only transport cargo, not units.
Construct a [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]UFO[COLOR_REVERT] to seize precious cargo from the Earthlings without revealing our involvement.
Aliens can construct [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Carriers[COLOR_REVERT] to move goods in bulk, though they are vulnerable to attack from dedicated naval units.
Construct a [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Cloaked Warship[COLOR_REVERT] to take the Earthling vessels by surprise.
Construct a massive [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Battlestar[COLOR_REVERT] to ensure our planet remains safe from Earthling attack.

[COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Hydrocarbons[COLOR_REVERT] are required to construct specific Earth units, such as [LINK=UNIT_WAGON_TRAIN]Convoys[\LINK], and to unlock essential structures like the [LINK=BUILDING_POWER_PLANT]Power Plant[\LINK] or [LINK=BUILDING_OIL_REFINERY]Oil Refinery[\LINK]. Additionally, they can be sold back on Earth for a profit. Since Alien Civilizations [COLOR_WARNING_TEXT]cannot[COLOR_REVERT] extract hydrocarbons themselves, purchasing this resource is vital for them throughout most of the game.

[COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Palanquins[COLOR_REVERT] are used by Alien Civilizations to transport goods over land, replacing Earth [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]Convoys[COLOR_REVERT]. While they are much slower than their Earthling counterparts, they offer invisibility and cheap, fast deployment. These advantages make them a viable alternative to the [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]aliens'[COLOR_REVERT] [COLOR_MAGENTA]amphibious[COLOR_REVERT] [COLOR_UNIT_TEXT]spaceships[COLOR_REVERT], which are otherwise the superior form of transportation.
